```{r}
#| label: setup
#| context: setup
library(shiny)
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(DT)
library(lubridate)

# Make the logo available to the live Shiny server.
addResourcePath("www", normalizePath("www"))

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

# Use this message when the selected filters leave no records.
empty_plot <- function() {
  plotly_empty() %>%
    layout(title = list(text = "No records match these inputs.", y = .5),
           xaxis = list(visible = FALSE), yaxis = list(visible = FALSE))
}

# This file contains the complete records from the course Adult Census data.
df <- read_csv("adult_census_clean.csv") %>%
  mutate(sex = factor(sex), education = factor(education), workclass = factor(workclass),
         income = factor(income, levels = c("<=50K", ">50K")))
```

# Plots

## {.sidebar}

Choose an education level. The two plots and the Data page use the selected records.

```{r}
#| label: sidebar-inputs
selectInput("education", "Education level",
            choices = c("All education levels" = "All", levels(df$education)),
            selected = "All")

textOutput("selection_note")
```

## Row

```{r}
#| label: plot-one-output
#| title: "Age distribution by sex"
#| fill: true
plotlyOutput("p1")
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-two-output
#| title: "Weekly work hours by income"
#| fill: true
plotlyOutput("p2")
```

# Data

```{r}
#| label: table-output
#| title: "Searchable data for the current selection"
#| fill: true
DTOutput("tbl")
```

# Data Notes

::: {.card title="Data and interpretation"}

These dashboards use the same Adult Census Income source file as the
earlier assignments, rather than Titanic. The original file has 32,561
records; 2,399 records with missing entries (including question marks) were
removed, leaving 30,162 complete records. Only the six columns needed here
are kept in the bundled CSV.

The first plot counts records in five-year age bins, separated by sex. The
second compares weekly work-hour distributions by income group. The line
inside each box is the median. Differences are descriptive; the counts
are not population-adjusted rates or evidence of causal effects.

**Source:** [Course Adult Census dataset](https://bryantstats.github.io/math421/data/adult_census.csv).

The inputs on Plots also filter the searchable table on Data. Include
`adult_census_clean.csv` and `logo.png` when publishing the QMD.

:::

```{r}
#| label: server
#| context: server
filtered <- reactive({
  req(input$education)
  if (input$education == "All") {
    df
  } else {
    df %>% filter(education == input$education)
  }
})

output$selection_note <- renderText({
  paste(format(nrow(filtered()), big.mark = ","), "records selected")
})

# Plot 1: Show age counts for the selected records.
output$p1 <- renderPlotly({
  d <- filtered()
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(empty_plot())
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = age, fill = sex)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, position = "identity", alpha = .6) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Female" = "#E07A5F", "Male" = "#3D7EA6")) +
    labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Records", fill = "Sex")
  ggplotly(p)
})

# Plot 2: Compare the median and spread of recorded weekly work hours.
output$p2 <- renderPlotly({
  d <- filtered()
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(empty_plot())
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = income, y = hours.per.week)) +
    geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue", outlier.alpha = .3) +
    labs(x = "Income group", y = "Work hours per week")
  ggplotly(p)
})

output$tbl <- renderDT({
  filtered() %>%
    select(age, sex, education, workclass, hours.per.week, income) %>%
    datatable(rownames = FALSE,
              colnames = c("Age", "Sex", "Education", "Work class", "Hours/week", "Income"),
              options = list(pageLength = 10, paging = TRUE, searching = TRUE,
                   dom = "lftip", scrollX = TRUE,
                   language = list(info = "Showing _START_ to _END_ of _TOTAL_ records",
                                   infoFiltered = "(filtered from _MAX_ total records)")))
}, server = TRUE)
```
